review_material.assessment: The source provides two temperature branches (T=10^-6 and T=1) for the incompressible kinetic energy E_i versus quench time tau_Q, with fitted power laws and explicit parameter values. The selected cluster is the incompressible kinetic energy scaling at equilibration time, which is supported by the main text and End Matter. The source reports fitted exponents and amplitudes for both branches, and the reviewer figure evidence confirms the applicability interval [100,1000] for both branches. The case is authoring-ready with one control (tau_Q), one readout (E_i), and two claims (one per temperature branch).

mechanisms.statement: The incompressible kinetic energy E_i at equilibration time scales with quench duration as E_i proportional to tau_Q^{-(1+2 nu)/(1+z nu)}, with mean-field exponents nu=1/2 and z=2 giving E_i proportional to tau_Q^{-1}. This follows from approximating E_i as a sum of isolated vortex contributions, each scaling with the KZ correlation length and background density.

review_material.paper_scope: The paper studies spontaneous quantum turbulence (SQT) in a 2D Bose-Einstein condensate formed by a thermal quench, using stochastic projected Gross-Pitaevskii simulations. It establishes Kibble-Zurek scaling of vortex number and equilibration time, Kolmogorov scaling of the incompressible kinetic energy spectrum, and universal collapse of spectra under KZ rescaling. The selected cluster focuses on the incompressible kinetic energy E_i at equilibration time as a function of quench duration tau_Q, with two temperature branches (T=10^-6 and T=1).

anchors.support: Definition of E_i as (1/2) integral |u_i(r, t_eq)|^2 d^2r = integral E_i(k) dk.
Each data point averaged over R=2000 (T=10^-6) and R=1000 (T=1) stochastic realizations; error bars denote 1 standard deviation.

readouts.definition: Incompressible kinetic energy at equilibration time, defined as E_i = (1/2) integral |u_i(r, t_eq)|^2 d^2r, where u_i is the incompressible (solenoidal) component of the density-weighted velocity field.

readouts.uncertainty: Error bars denote 1 standard deviation; fit uncertainties are reported as plus/minus values with unspecified meaning (source_unspecified).
